objective: Assessing initial program objectives, requirements, and risks against the organization's strategic plan, vision, and mission
secondaryObjectives: Developing and evaluating the program's business case: feasibility, readiness, and strategic alignment
Obtaining organizational leadership approval via a program charter (high-level costs, milestones, benefits)

sources.cite: PMI, Program Management Professional (PgMP) Examination Content Outline: Strategic Program Alignment 15%, Program Life Cycle Management 44%, Benefits Management 11%, Stakeholder Engagement 16%, Governance 14%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17. The domain weights were confirmed through a summarizing fetch of a training provider's article (eartech.pmtraining.com, 'How to Prepare for the PgMP Certification Exam'), which describes Program Life Cycle Management as 'initiating, planning, executing, controlling, and closing the program across its phases' and Governance as 'the boards, gates, and decision rights that let leadership steer and, when needed, stop a program'. PMI's own outline PDF did not come up in search and PMI's PgMP pages read today do not list the domains; the task wording is the course seed's, to verify against PMI's PDF. The organization, the portfolio or program, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are asked to shape a crane automation program for Saltwick Port Authority, a fictional port. The board's strategy: grow container throughput 30% by 2032 while cutting emissions and keeping local employment.
handover: The equipment vendor's proposal promises 50% labor savings.
The union has a no-redundancy agreement until 2030.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a fortnight at a time. A decision comes to you at each board meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Meeting 2: the union learns of the labor-cut objective and threatens action; the board pauses the program.
Meeting 3: the CFO asks for the case; without it, the board refuses the charter for another quarter.
Meeting 4: the board refuses to ratify the order; cancelling it costs a 9 million dollar penalty.

alignPrompt.title: Do the objectives fit the strategy?
alignPrompt.context: The vendor frames the program as labor cuts.

choices.label: Reframe objectives around throughput and emissions, with workforce redeployment and training, and flag labor cuts as conflicting with the agreement and the strategy
choices.feedback: Program objectives are checked against strategy, mission and constraints before anything else.

choices.label: Keep labor savings and add throughput
choices.feedback: Labor savings still conflict with the agreement.

choices.label: Adopt the vendor's labor-savings objective
choices.feedback: It breaches the union agreement and the local-jobs goal.

casePrompt.title: Quantifying the benefits
casePrompt.context: Throughput and emissions benefits aren't quantified.

choices.label: A business case quantifying throughput (+22%), emissions (-15%), costs, feasibility and readiness (skills, power supply), with a high-level cost-benefit analysis

effects.log: The case quantifies benefits and readiness.

choices.feedback: The business case tests feasibility and readiness and quantifies the benefits that serve the strategy.

choices.label: Use the vendor's figures
choices.feedback: Unchallenged figures for the wrong benefit.

choices.label: Skip the case: the board likes automation
choices.feedback: Nothing to approve or measure against.

charterPrompt.title: Getting authorized
charterPrompt.context: The sponsor wants to start buying cranes now.

choices.label: Present a charter with high-level costs, milestones, benefits and governance to the board for approval before any commitment
choices.feedback: A program is authorized by leadership through its charter before committing funds.

choices.label: Get the sponsor's approval by email
choices.feedback: The board, which owns the strategy, hasn't authorized it.

choices.label: Sign the crane order now to lock the price
choices.feedback: Committing 90 million dollars before the program is authorized is outside your authority.

reflection.question: Write the program charter's cover note for the board.

parts.label: Alignment and case
parts.criteria: Throughput and emissions objectives; labor cuts excluded; quantified benefits and readiness.
parts.modelAnswer: The program grows throughput 22% and cuts emissions 15%, redeploying staff in line with the agreement; the case covers costs, feasibility and readiness.

parts.label: Authorization
parts.criteria: The charter approved before any order.
parts.modelAnswer: We ask you to approve the charter; no order is placed before it.

source.note: No risk above appetite at the close without a treatment.

scoring.modelReasoning: Program definition starts by assessing objectives against the strategy, mission and constraints. The business case quantifies the benefits that serve the strategy and tests feasibility and readiness. Leadership authorizes the program through a charter (costs, milestones, benefits) before commitments are made.
